accepted.evidence: Turner explicitly records European Romani vušt 'lip' under ṓṣṭha; the source prints vušt in its unchanged-singular/plural noun list (p. 131 §3.1.8). Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives European Romani dives and Palula dīs under divasá. The source explicitly contrasts Zargari singular dis and plural dise (p. 131 §3.1.8); the plural is an ordinary inflection of the same inherited stem. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives southeastern European Romani čhib 'tongue' under jihvā́. The source expressly lists čhiba as the plural of čhib (p. 131 §3.1.8); its singular already has a reviewed 5228 link. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner explicitly gives Greek and Hungarian Romani muy 'mouth, face' under múkha; Zargari muj 'face; mouth' is printed in the irregular-plural list (p. 132 §3.1.9). Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives European Romani bakro, feminine bakri 'sheep' under bárkara. Rezaibaghbidi prints bakri 'sheep' in §2.3.3 and repeats it in §3.2.1, distinct from the same etymon's widespread later 'goat' sense. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner gives southeastern European Romani čhavo 'boy' under *chāpa. The source prints Zargari čhā and its irregular plural čhāvu (p. 132 §3.1.9), preserving its own truncation and plural vowel; Turner's deeper relationship to śāva remains unclear. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

The source identifies Zargari phorāl as < Early Romani phral and explains its inserted vowel by Zargari CV(CC) syllable structure (p. 129 §2.4.1).
